name: OVR Technology
old_description: OVR has unlocked scent for video games with the Omara Scent Display.
about:
OVR Technology is based in Burlington, Vermont, where a multidisciplinary team of industrial designers, fragrance designers, neuroscientists, and software engineers developed the Omara Scent Display, a personal device that brings olfactory immersion to video games.

The company produces two models: the Omara Core, a desktop scent display with ten scent channels priced at $179, and the Omara Pro, a portable advanced display with sixteen channels priced at $649. Both units combine hardware, proprietary scent cartridges or cassettes, and software to deliver scent in burst or continuous modes, with a time-to-perception ranging from 500 to 1,000 milliseconds.

OVR Technology serves the video gaming and virtual reality markets, targeting both end users—gamers seeking deeper immersion—and creators, including independent game studios worldwide that partner with the company to integrate scent into their titles.

The venture was driven by the ambition to add a missing sensory layer to digital experiences, summarized by the company's statement that "gaming has never felt more alive" and its willingness to tackle the difficulty of being first in digital scent technology.

name: OXOS Medical, Inc
old_description: OXOS is transforming medical imaging with innovative, portable X‑ray solutions
about:
OXOS Medical, Inc. was founded in June 2016 in Atlanta, Georgia, as Micro C, LLC, before adopting its current name. The company was started by Evan M. Ruff, a computer engineer and MBA from Georgia Tech, and Dr. Gregory P. Kolovich, a reconstructive hand surgeon trained at Harvard Medical School. Kolovich's frustration with the traditional imaging process during surgery sparked the idea for a portable dynamic digital radiography device.

The company develops and manufactures portable X‑ray systems, including the Micro C and the newer MC2, both cleared by the U.S. FDA under 510(k). The devices are designed for low radiation exposure, modular portability, and a no‑fire positioning system that optimizes alignment. A proprietary software module called AiLARA automates dose optimization per the ALARA principle. The team comprises engineers, designers, and clinical advisors, though headcount and facility size are not disclosed.

OXOS serves orthopedics, pediatrics, and sports medicine, selling directly to clinics, hospitals, and surgical practices. Testimonials cite use by hand and upper‑extremity surgeons, foot‑and‑ankle specialists, and team physicians for professional sports organizations such as the Jacksonville Jaguars. The systems are marketed for point‑of‑need imaging in diverse care settings.

The founders state the mission is to let anyone, anywhere access radiographic diagnostics at the point of need. They emphasize three pillars: safety through low‑dose profiles, simplicity via portable and modular design, and intelligence through real‑time alignment and automated dose control.

Oceanside Welding & Fabrication operates from Oakland Park, Florida, serving Broward and Palm Beach counties. The company was started by Jerry Menagh, who brought years of hands-on welding and aluminum fabrication experience to a small local operation that has grown into a family-owned shop.

Customers include homeowners, builders, and property managers throughout South Florida, as well as marine clients needing pontoon repairs and landscaping or pressure-washing businesses requiring custom trailers. The company's work is tailored to withstand the region's coastal climate.

Menagh founded the business on a principle of doing the job right with pride, emphasizing craftsmanship, integrity, reliability, safety, and community. The company highlights transparent quoting, dependable timelines, and a fully welded, powder-coated product built for Florida's environment as key differentiators.

The mill provides custom fiber processing for customers who supply their own wool, and it produces 100% Hawaiian-grown and processed yarn. name: Ohio Semitronics, Inc.
old_description: New or Obsolete Product | Ready to Test Prototypes in Just 3 Weeks
about:
Ohio Semitronics, Inc. was founded in 1964 in Hilliard, Ohio, where it pioneered the first Hall Effect electrical measurement devices. The company has remained a U.S.-based manufacturer of custom transducers and sensors for over six decades.

The company designs and builds a broad line of standard transducers — including AC/DC current, AC/DC voltage, watt-VAR, multifunction, frequency, and power factor models — as well as signal conditioners, relays, integrators, and panel meters. Its core business is custom engineering: Ohio Semitronics takes measurement concepts from discussion to working prototype in two to six weeks, leveraging CAD and 3D printing to accelerate development.

Its devices serve petroleum and petrochemical plants, electric utilities, solar and wind installations, test and measurement labs, automation and control systems, and naval surface and subsurface programs. The company has been a key resource for organizations such as Battelle Institute, Bell Labs, and the U.S. Department of Defense.

Ohio Semitronics differentiates itself through deep expertise in the physics of electrical measurement, an ability to engineer unique devices for the most challenging applications, and a track record of delivering custom prototypes in as little as three weeks.

name: Ohio Woodworking Co
old_description: From precision machining to high-quality finishing, our team delivers consistency, accuracy, and scalability—helping you keep production on schedule and up to standard.
about:
Ohio Woodworking Company operates from a facility near downtown Cincinnati, Ohio, on the same site where German immigrant William Frank founded the business in 1930 after apprenticing as a cabinetmaker. Now a third-generation, family-owned firm, leadership has passed from Frank to his son Tom and then to Tom’s son Tom Jr. and son-in-law Richard, who together bring over 27 years of cabinetmaking expertise.

The shop combines CNC machinery and AutoCAD-based drafting with traditional woodworking tools to produce custom millwork and cabinetry for commercial and institutional spaces. Capabilities range from one-of-a-kind custom builds to large-scale production runs, covering architectural millwork, commercial casework, retail fixtures, bank teller lines, salon displays, university furniture, residential cabinetry, and kitchen and food service stations. A dedicated team—many with decades of experience—supports the full design-to-execution process alongside architects, designers, and trades.

The company serves banking, retail, salon, higher education, medical office, and food service sectors. Long-standing clients include U.S. Bank, which relies on Ohio Woodworking for branch fixtures and casework. Projects also encompass medical office reception areas, salon and service area furniture, and custom residential work, all engineered to precise specifications.

Ohio Woodworking emphasizes values of quality, ingenuity, perseverance, humor, and family—principles the firm says are built into every project. By blending time-tested techniques with modern technology, the company aims to deliver precision, reliability, and smart custom solutions that sustain decades-long partnerships.

Olan Plastics runs multiple injection molding machines ranging from 85 to 610 tons, processing a wide variety of resins and rubber. Warehousing and drop-shipping services round out the offering.

The company serves customers across various industries, from startups to established firms. A noted example is Carton Flow Slotting Systems, which uses Olan Plastics to manufacture components that optimize order-picking systems in distribution and fulfillment centers throughout North America.

Olan Plastics emphasizes statistical process control and strict quality procedures aimed at defect-free processing, and positions itself as a cost-effective solution provider with short lead times and on-time delivery.

old_description: Axial-flux in-wheel electric motors for EVs
about:
Orbis Electric is based in Santa Rosa, California. The company was founded by Marcus Hays (CEO/CTO), Chance Claxton (COO/CMO), and Scott Streeter (Manufacturing Director) on a vision to revolutionize electric propulsion through advanced axial-flux permanent-magnet motor technology. Its origins trace to electric mobility, where the team developed Ring Drive Wheel technology and completed a four-year validation program with Volkswagen Group in Germany.

Today Orbis produces axial-flux in-wheel motors, modular liquid-cooling platforms (COOL·E), and high-efficiency electric drive systems for propulsion, power generation, and thermal management. The COOL·E platform integrates automotive- and defense-grade motor technology, advanced power electronics, and intelligent orchestrated controls with predictive diagnostics to deliver megawatt-scale liquid cooling. Manufacturing processes include additive manufacturing, CNC machining, and casting, supported by a portfolio of 16 issued patents and 40 pending applications.

The company serves electric mobility (Volkswagen Group), transport refrigeration (eTRU), defense propulsion, and AI data-center operators. Its cooling systems are designed for the transition to 800V DC-native architectures used by cloud infrastructure providers. Collaborations with Ames National Laboratory and Oak Ridge National Laboratory on Cerium Gap and MAGMA magnetic materials further extend its reach into critical-materials research.

Orbis was started to bring EV-derived drive technology into data-center cooling, arguing that legacy HVAC approaches cannot match the efficiency and response speed of automotive-grade systems. The firm emphasizes a DC-native, power-agnostic platform that recovers power, reclaims white space, and protects uptime, while its national-lab partnerships aim to reduce reliance on scarce critical minerals.

about:
Pacific Allied Products Ltd. was founded in 1965 in Kapolei, Hawaii, initially producing wall panels and Hawaiian Ice Coolers from expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam. The company began as a local manufacturer of foam products and later expanded into recreational items such as surfboards and swim rings.

Today the company operates a vertically integrated facility spanning over 90,000 square feet of manufacturing and warehouse space with approximately 50 employees. It produces both EPS foam products — including insulation boards, contoured tapered tile, and drainage boards for construction — and PET packaging, running preform production, blow molding, bottle filling, capping, labeling, shrink wrapping, and palletizing on a single site. Annual bottle capacity exceeds 200 million units, and recent filler and blow-molding upgrades have raised output by more than 60 percent.

The business serves Hawaii’s beverage industry, supplying PET bottles for soda, juice, milk, and water brands, as well as the construction and roofing sector with specialized foam insulation and roofing components. It also co-packs bottled water for local brands, positioning itself as the only island facility that handles preforms, blow molding, and co-packaging under one roof.

Pacific Allied Products emphasizes food safety and quality management, holding ISO 9001 and FSSC 22000 certifications. Its stated mission is to be Hawaii’s plastic manufacturer through a commitment to excellence for employees and shareholders, and it highlights its integrated management system covering food safety, quality, environmental, and safety aspects.

Pacific Medical runs four divisions: OrthoLIFE, a proprietary patient-centered orthopedic rehabilitation and recovery platform; Surgical, providing innovative solutions for orthopedic and surgical care; Biologics, delivering advanced regenerative and biologic products; and Top Shelf Orthopedics, supporting product design, management, and distribution within the orthopedic space.

Pacific Medical serves healthcare providers, hospitals, and patients across the orthopedic continuum. Its customer base includes hospitals and clinical practices in 18 states, with the company reporting 540,000 lives changed in the most recent year. The firm specializes in orthopedic rehabilitation, arthroscopic surgery, sports medicine, prosthetics, and orthotics, positioning itself as a extension of its partners' practices.

The company emphasizes enduring partnerships built on trust, responsiveness, and a shared dedication to improving the quality of patient care. Its OrthoLIFE platform is designed to streamline care, improve outcomes, and support the unique needs of each facility, reflecting a stated commitment to innovation with integrity and partnerships with purpose.

name: Paricon Technologies
old_description: We’re a leading designer and manufacturer of state-of-the-art
about:
Paricon Technologies Corporation operates from Taunton, Massachusetts, where it designs and manufactures elastomeric interconnect solutions for the electronics industry. The company has invested heavily in proprietary product and process technologies over its history, though a founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company's core offering centers on its PariPoser® anisotropic elastomer fabric, a material engineered for bandwidths exceeding 110 GHz that behaves as a lumped parameter with inductance below 0.1 nH. Paricon translates this technology into a range of interconnect products including die-cut material, adjustable swivel-top sockets, clamshell sockets, compact manual-loading sockets, double-latch sockets, flex-to-board assemblies, and board-to-board connectors. It also provides PariProbe® probe solutions that combine elastomers with short solid pins for BGA applications, supported by optional Peltier or liquid cooling for thermal management.

Paricon serves customers in test and measurement, microwave and RF, wafer testing, custom connector applications, and high-speed digital electronics. Its solutions are used in applications requiring reliable high-frequency contacts, such as RF waveguides, large BGA probing, and advanced semiconductor test.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative elastomeric interconnect solutions that enable customers to push the boundaries of electronics design and manufacturing. Its vision targets global leadership in high-performance interconnects, grounded in core values of innovation, quality, customer focus, and excellence. Paricon emphasizes continuous R&D investment in proprietary technologies to stay ahead of industry needs.

Parkman Woodworks was founded in 2015 on Parkman Avenue in Silverlake, Los Angeles, by Graham Taglang, who remains the public face of the company. The venture began with a pickup truck and a thousand dollars, building its first pieces from sustainable wood in a friend's driveway. In 2019 the operation moved into a historic brick-and-timber textile mill a building that marked its 100th anniversary in 2023, with a roof framed in the same antique timber the shop uses for furniture.

The company produces custom wood-and-steel furniture—conference tables, dining tables, bed frames, desks, coffee tables, bookshelves, consoles, benches, mantels, countertops, and restaurant pieces—entirely in-house. A team of six craftspeople handles design, woodworking, welding, and powder-coating of low-carbon iron, working from the 100-year-old facility. Materials are sourced hyperlocally: solid hardwoods recovered from naturally fallen Southern California trees and structures.

Parkman serves both residential and commercial clients. Its furniture furnishes corporate offices, home offices, dining rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, living rooms, and restaurants. Trade and custom-order channels supply interior designers, architects, and direct consumers seeking bespoke pieces.

The founding mission is to turn wasted wood into practical art while advancing the values of handcraft. The shop emphasizes accountability, awareness, and achievement, with every piece passing through the full in-house build process from design to delivery.

Payoff Solar is based in South Jordan, Utah, and was founded in 2024 by Matt Newman, JD McBride, and Kip Denning. The company began with a mission to make solar energy accessible, affordable, and hassle-free for homeowners and businesses, focusing on a financial payoff within three to four years rather than the industry-typical 15 to 20.

The company supplies high-efficiency solar panels and advanced battery storage systems, and provides full-service installation that covers consultation, site assessment, system design, permitting, and final inspection. Pricing is advertised at $1.50 per watt, roughly half the $3–4 per watt commonly quoted by other installers, and customers can choose to perform some of the work themselves to reduce cost further.

Payoff Solar serves residential and commercial customers seeking to reduce energy bills and carbon footprint. Its process is structured in three steps: a quick property and needs assessment, a detailed proposal with specifications and projected savings, and professional installation handled from permits through inspection.

The founders state the business was started to close the gap between solar’s environmental benefits and its financial return, aiming to make systems pay for themselves in five years or less. Core values cited are innovation, sustainability, and affordability, with an emphasis on flexible financing and competitive pricing.

about:
Performance Systems Integration, doing business as PSI Conversions, operates from Brick Township, New Jersey. The company’s origins trace back more than two decades to the development of its first standalone wiring harness for LS engine swaps, built on a combined 25-plus years of automotive electrical experience.

PSI designs and manufactures plug-and-play wiring harnesses for General Motors Gen II through Gen V LS and LT engines, including the LT1/LT4, LS1/LS6, Vortec, LS2, LS3, LS7, and LT/Ecotec3 families. Harnesses are assembled in-house using high-temperature cross-linked TXL or GXL wire, ultrasonic-welded splices, fusible-link protection, and OEM-specification terminals from suppliers such as Delphi/Aptiv, Yazaki, and Kostal. Each harness is wrapped in high-temp tape and either F6 PET braid or nylon split loom, then 100% functionally tested on computer-controlled Dynalab or Cirris equipment. Beyond harnesses, PSI supplies engine controller kits, transmission components, fuel systems, gauge clusters, and a curated selection of partner brands including Holley, Vintage Air, Dakota Digital, and HPTuners.

The company serves the automotive aftermarket, targeting professional installers, restoration shops, and individual builders performing LS/LT swaps into a wide range of platforms—Chevrolet, Ford, Nissan, Jeep, Toyota, and classic hot rods. A dealer program extends reach to retail and installation partners.

PSI emphasizes domestic production, rapid fulfillment (in-stock harnesses ship in one to three business days), and direct technical support available five days a week by phone and 24/7 by email. The original harness layout, developed for simplified ground and power routing, has become a de facto standard in the LS-swap community.

name: Petoskey Plastics Inc
old_description: To earn the appreciation and respect of our customers, associates, and communities.
about:
Petoskey Plastics operates from its corporate headquarters in McKinney, Texas, but traces its roots to Petoskey, Michigan, where Duke and Paul Keiswetter founded the company in 1969. The privately held, family-owned business began with five employees and a single bag machine converting purchased film into plastic bags. By 1975 the founders had added an extrusion line to produce their own film, setting the stage for a vertically integrated operation that now spans four U.S. manufacturing sites.

Today the company runs facilities in Petoskey, Michigan; Morristown, Tennessee; Hartford City, Indiana; and McKinney, Texas, employing roughly 500 associates. Its core processes include 3- and 5-layer blown film extrusion, bag converting, shrink film production, and a 330,000-square-foot recycling plant in Indiana that feeds post-consumer resin back into the extrusion lines. A 4-color offset paper printing press at the Morristown site adds packaging capabilities. In-house quality labs at each location support consistent output.

Petoskey serves automotive, construction, medical, retail, institutional, packaging, janitorial, parks and recreation, and fundraising markets, with products sold in 45 countries. Customers range from private-label brands to OEMs seeking custom-engineered polyethylene solutions, including films with up to 70 percent third-party certified post-consumer recycled content that exceed EPA requirements.

The company’s differentiation rests on its closed-loop recycling model, veteran-owned status, and a family-culture that emphasizes hands-on management. After receiving the National Veteran Business Development Council’s Veteran Business of the Year award in 2023 and 2025, Petoskey continues to position its sustainable polyethylene as a lower-carbon alternative for flexible packaging.

about:
Phoenix Solar Panel Systems operates from Phoenix, Arizona, serving the metropolitan area and offering services nationwide through a network of installation partners. The company was founded by Steven Smith, J.D., known as "Solar Steve Esquire," after he worked at several Valley solar companies and observed what he describes as a lack of professionalism and regulation in the industry. Smith established the business to prioritize honesty, integrity, and transparency in residential solar.

The company does not perform installations directly. Instead, it helps homeowners and businesses evaluate solar options — grid-tied systems, off-grid designs, battery backup, and commercial arrays — and connects them with independent, licensed installers. Customers contract directly with the installer for the work. Phoenix Solar Panel Systems also offers home energy audits, solar water heater services, EV charger installation, attic insulation, duct sealing, and solar panel cleaning, removal, and reinstallation.

The firm serves residential homeowners and commercial property owners in Arizona, with a focus on the Phoenix metro area. It works with the state's major utilities, Arizona Public Service (APS) and Salt River Project (SRP), and guides clients through federal tax credits and Arizona-specific incentives. Commercial clients include businesses seeking to reduce operating costs through solar installations on rooftops or parking structures.

Smith states the company was started to "clean up the residential solar industry" by educating customers rather than selling to them, presenting both positives and negatives of solar ownership. The goal is long-term, mutually beneficial relationships with customers and employees, positioning the business as a consumer advocate in a market the founder characterizes as poorly regulated.

about:
Pick-Up City, an auto and truck recycler, has operated from Marion County, West Virginia since 1992. The company is headquartered in Fairmont and runs a 78,000-square-foot indoor warehouse in nearby White Hall. President Grant Kelly leads the business, which began as a local salvage operation and grew into a regional parts supplier.

The company dismantles late-model vehicles piece by piece, cleaning, testing, and cataloging each component into a computerized inventory that now exceeds 65,000 parts. Its bumper-to-bumper offering includes engines, transmissions, axles, doors, bumpers, windshields, fenders, lighting, clips, seats, and body panels. All parts are stored indoors away from the elements, and fluids such as freon, coolant, oil, gasoline, and brake fluid are recovered and recycled to meet environmental standards.

Pick-Up City serves automotive repair shops, collision centers, and individual vehicle owners throughout West Virginia and surrounding states, with nationwide shipping available via common carrier. Free regional delivery is offered for local customers, and the sales team provides parts lookup assistance both in person and by phone.

The business differentiates itself through its indoor, climate-controlled warehousing, a searchable digital catalog, and warranties of 30 to 90 days on select recycled parts. Its emphasis on environmentally responsible fluid disposal and the condition of parts — described as “as good as or better than the day they arrived” — reflects the founding goal of providing a reliable alternative to traditional junkyards.

The facility functions as both a plastics distributor and a fabrication shop. It stocks a wide range of sheet materials including acrylic, polycarbonate, nylon, acetal homopolymer and copolymer, fluorocarbon, UHMW, polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC, polystyrene, high-pressure laminates, and polyurethane. In-house fabrication capabilities cover CNC routing and laser cutting, milling, drilling, turning, straight or pattern cutting, welding (hot air and solvent), bonding (solvent and silicone), edging, buffing, sanding, grinding, sandblasting, and precision machining. Assembly services encompass mechanical fastening, welding, custom wiring harness assembly, bonding, riveting, and packing and shipping.

The branch serves customers throughout southern and central New Hampshire, with a listed service area that includes Manchester, Derry, Nashua, Salem, Merrimack, Hudson, Windham, Bedford, Amherst, Hooksett, and numerous other communities. Its molded components go into construction (weather‑resistant barriers, structural fittings), storage and logistics (impact‑resistant totes and bins), consumer goods (food‑grade, BPA‑free housewares), agriculture (irrigation parts), automotive (tight‑tolerance fittings), and medical (non‑invasive devices, with cleanroom capability available).

Norco emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015‑compliant quality system, backed by a Brown & Sharpe CMM capable of ±0.0001‑inch measurement, and its 50‑year track record as a family‑owned, full‑service partner that can handle projects from prototype through high‑volume runs.

about:
Plastics Unlimited operates from a 130,000-square-foot facility in Preston, Iowa. The company was founded in 1993 by Terry, Nancy, and Gene Kieffer on their family farm after the physical toll of livestock farming prompted them to seek a less labor-intensive venture. They purchased a used thermoforming machine at auction, installed it in a machine shed, and began producing thermoformed parts.

Today the manufacturer provides custom thermoforming, composites, and urethane molding, supported by in-house design and tooling, CAD services, and robotic CNC trimming. The facility houses multiple thermoforming machines capable of handling both small and large parts, and the company's proprietary TEC® (Tooless Engineered Composites) process combines plastics and composites to produce Class-A surfaces with reduced tooling. Secondary operations and assembly are also offered.

The company serves agriculture, construction, dunnage, material handling, medical, OEM, outdoor/recreation, aerospace, industrial, and transportation markets. Its agricultural roots give it particular insight into farm equipment components, while its composites and urethane capabilities address medical device housings, construction equipment hoods, and returnable packaging for industrial clients.

The founders chose thermoforming for its lower entry cost compared to injection molding and built the business on farming values—planet stewardship, quality, innovation, a can-do attitude, and customer service. Plastics Unlimited emphasizes green innovation, award-winning quality, and faster turnaround times than alternative plastic processes.

about:
Popknot Wood operates from Rogers, Arkansas. The business traces its roots to founder John, a U.S. Army veteran, who began teaching his grandchildren woodworking in his shop. What started as birdhouses and simple boxes grew into a family-driven venture; together they built a business plan and launched Popknot Wood. The company is proudly veteran-owned and family-operated.

The shop delivers custom woodworking, furniture restoration, and precision CNC and laser work. Capabilities include custom-built wood products, replacement of broken or discontinued parts, heirloom repairs, and a range of specialty items such as cutting boards (including state-shaped designs), wooden urns and memorial pieces, awards and presentation pieces, river tables, custom flags, and signs. Production is carried out in a small workshop that sources local wood whenever possible and ships finished pieces to all 50 states.

Customers include individuals seeking one-of-a-kind furniture repairs or personalized gifts, families commissioning memorial urns or heirloom restorations, and faith-based organizations such as churches and ministries looking for purpose-built pieces. The shop also serves buyers of awards, presentation items, and custom signage.

John credits his Army service for instilling discipline and integrity that carry into every build. He views craftsmanship as stewardship — using given gifts to create meaningful, lasting work. The business began as a way to teach creativity, responsibility, and entrepreneurship to the next generation, and that legacy remains central to its purpose.

Porter Barn Wood operates from Phoenix, Arizona. The business was founded in 2010 by Thomas Porter, who started the venture with the help of his friend Craig Suiter after using a forklift to unload a shipment of reclaimed barn wood and recognizing local demand for such materials. Porter formed the LLC in 2012 and opened a showroom that now serves both walk-in customers and commercial clients.

The company runs a wood shop, metal shop, concrete shop, and finishing/contracting teams, enabling it to fabricate custom furniture, architectural elements, lighting, and millwork. Core processes include CNC plasma cutting, CNC routing, laser engraving, blacksmithing, milling, spindle duplication, and production manufacturing. Design services cover 3D CAD, concept rendering, and furniture design, while finishing options span lacquer, polyurethane, conversion varnish, waxes, oils, and custom finish matching. The facility features evap-cooled and air-conditioned workshops and handles projects ranging from small DIY pieces to large commercial build-outs.

Porter Barn Wood serves restaurant and hospitality clients — such as Surf City, Lazy Bird, and Famè — as well as commercial contractors, residential remodelers, architects, and builders. The shop has also hosted film and television productions for HGTV and PBS specials. In addition, the company supplies reclaimed materials to DIY enthusiasts and runs free community classes and demonstrations.

Porter describes the operation as a family business focused on growing while keeping high-quality reclaimed materials at reasonable prices. A stated differentiator is the willingness to incorporate customers' own reclaimed materials — whether from a family barn, old warehouse, or unique finds — into custom projects, and the ability to provide design, fabrication, and installation under one roof.

about:
Portsmouth Fabric Company has operated in the historic downtown district of Portsmouth, New Hampshire since 1980, after its founding in 1979 as a source for natural-fiber fabrics, fashion fabrics, and designer cuts. The shop moved to its current location a year after opening and began featuring Bernina sewing machines in 1980, expanding into contemporary quilting fabrics and fiber-arts books in 1990. Today the inventory spans more than 7,000 bolts of fabric.

The store stocks a broad range of textiles including contemporary quilting cottons, Bali batiks, silk dupioni, silk noil, silk organza, silk charmeuse, flannels, batiste, cotton solids, laminates, linens, velvets, and wool. It is an authorized Bernina dealer offering the full line of Swiss-made machines — from the Liberty 495 and 580 to the 770 Plus, 990, and Q-Series longarms — with free, unlimited guide classes and on-site service by a Bernina-trained technician. The shop also carries specialty threads from Aurifil, Isacord, Mettler, and Superior, plus trims, ribbons, buttons, and notions. A dedicated classroom hosts scheduled workshops with visiting artists such as Kaffe Fassett and Brandon Mably, and the space is available for private rental for sewing retreats.

Customers range from individual quilters and garment sewists to fiber-art groups and workshop attendees. The shop serves the New England quilting and sewing community through two annual clearance events — an Anniversary Sale in early July and a Year-End Clearance in late December — and has supported local charities including New Generation, a shelter for homeless pregnant women.

The company emphasizes professional advice and individualized product selection, a service model it has maintained for over four decades.

Power Control Services is based in Broussard, Louisiana. The company traces its roots to 1996 when Walter Bergeron founded Synergy Technologies in his backyard. The business was later renamed Power Control Services and remains family-owned.

The firm specializes in industrial electronic repair and rebuild, servomotor repair, and component-level restoration of automation equipment such as AC/DC drives, servo drives, PLCs, power supplies, and industrial displays. Technicians work at ESD- and SMT-equipped repair stations using a proactive process that replaces failed parts with high-reliability components and applies protective coatings for future serviceability. The shop offers snapshot reporting, in-service warranty coverage, and technical support, serving customers nationwide through a network of industrial distributors.

Its customer base spans power generation (Entergy), food processing (Tyson Foods, Coca‑Cola), oil and gas (Parker Drilling, NOV, Transocean, Halliburton, Schlumberger), chemical manufacturing (Dow), and major end users such as ConocoPhillips in Alaska and Disney World in Florida. The company also partners with regional and national distributors to extend its reach.

Power Control Services was created because the founders believed original equipment manufacturers prioritize new sales over durable, repairable designs. The company differentiates itself with a five‑day standard turnaround, pricing 35‑50 % below competitor rates, generous warranties, certified technicians, and an extensive online portal for tracking and documentation.

about:
Power Factor was founded in March 2013 in Baltimore, Maryland, by master electrician George Lang IV. After graduating from Eastern Vocational Technical High School in 1995 and completing an apprenticeship with Associated Builders and Contractors, Lang ran the electrical maintenance department at Johns Hopkins Hospital before joining a Maryland solar firm as a partner. There he designed a Positive Train Control system and a patented battery system deployed in war zones for the U.S. military. When that company was sold, Lang brought five key employees with him to launch Power Factor as a family-owned solar and electrical contractor.

The company provides full-service solar and electrical installation, repair, replacement, and maintenance for residential, commercial, and industrial properties. With over 60 employees and $18 million in annual sales, Power Factor has completed more than 2,100 residential installations and deployed over 43 megawatts of solar capacity across the United States and abroad. Its crews are OSHA-certified and handle projects ranging from rooftop arrays and battery storage to EV charging stations, LEED-certified lighting retrofits, and general electrical construction.

Customers include homeowners throughout the Baltimore region, businesses seeking to reduce energy costs, and federal agencies — notably the Department of Defense, for which the firm has delivered over 35 megawatts of PV projects. The company also serves the telecommunications sector and works on commercial solar developments nationwide.

Lang started Power Factor to bring reliable, transparent solar and electrical services to communities, drawing on his experience building mission-critical power systems for the military. The company emphasizes no hidden fees, 24/7 emergency response, and NABCEP-certified technicians, aiming to complete every project on time and on budget.

PowerFilm Solar operates from Ames, Iowa, where it has designed and manufactured thin-film and crystalline solar panels for over three decades. The company focuses on custom-engineered solar solutions for commercial, government, and OEM platforms, with engineering and production capabilities based in the United States.

The company manufactures thin-film amorphous silicon solar panels using proprietary processes and assembles semi-flexible crystalline panels through controlled production. Its capabilities span panel construction, electrical integration, system-level validation, and full development from prototype through sustained production volumes. PowerFilm supports custom geometry, substrate selection, encapsulation, energy harvesting electronics, charge controllers, and application-specific mounting configurations.

PowerFilm serves commercial transportation fleets seeking to reduce idling and extend battery life for liftgates, telematics, APUs, and refrigeration; government and defense programs requiring portable, vehicle-mounted, and remote power; uncrewed maritime systems needing sealed, marine-grade surface generation; low-speed electric vehicle fleets on campuses and municipal sites; IoT and connected devices in remote environments; and consumer mobility applications. Past deployments include telematics, marine, IoT, U.S. military, and space exploration programs.

The company emphasizes application-specific design over catalog formats, controlled manufacturing with environmental and mechanical testing (vibration, temperature cycling, long-term outdoor exposure), and direct engineering collaboration from early development through deployment. Its U.S.-based thin-film production and crystalline assembly are cited as differentiators for programs requiring domestic sourcing and supply-chain control.

about:
Nasoya, now operating as Pulmuone Nasoya Foods USA, traces its roots to 1978 when its founders began producing tofu in a converted barn in Leominster, Massachusetts. In 2004, the brand was acquired by South Korea’s Pulmuone Foods, a global leader in plant-based foods, and the combined entity has since expanded its U.S. footprint. Today the company is headquartered in Ayer, Massachusetts, where a new facility slated to open in 2025 is expected to become the world’s largest tofu production line.

The company manufactures a range of plant-based products, including multiple tofu varieties (silken, firm, extra-firm, super-firm), Asian-inspired items such as noodles, dumplings, and wonton wraps, and ready-to-eat meals under the Plantspired label. Its operations emphasize organic, non-GMO soybeans sourced from local growers, and the facility incorporates sustainable practices such as tray-free packaging, brine recycling, and wastewater treatment that processes 34.6 million gallons annually. Historical data notes a 1987 facility capable of producing more than 60,000 pounds of tofu per week.

Nasoya’s products are distributed through more than 25,000 retail locations nationwide, primarily in grocery produce sections, serving both mainstream and natural-food retailers. The brand also engages foodservice and culinary channels through partnerships with institutions like the Culinary Institute of America.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a commitment to organic sourcing, environmental stewardship, and making plant-based eating accessible. Its mission centers on delivering wholesome, convenient foods that fit diverse lifestyles while reducing resource use—citing tofu’s 85% lower water footprint compared to beef.

Q&D Wire Cable Assembly Inc. operates in Hillsboro, Oregon, in the Silicon Forest region just west of Portland. The company traces its plastic molding expertise to a spin-off from Tektronix more than 50 years ago, originally located in Forest Grove before moving to its current Hillsboro facility in 2011. The cable assembly and contract assembly divisions have been serving local manufacturers since 2008.

The shop provides custom wire and cable assemblies, electrical and mechanical box builds, injection/compression/transfer plastic molding, and ECN rework and fulfillment services. It specializes in high-mix, low-to-medium volume production, handling wire sizes from 14 to 32 AWG, coaxial and ribbon cables, and a range of thermoplastic and thermoset materials. Processes include hand and semi-automatic crimping, lead-free soldering, epoxy potting, 100% electrical testing, and hipot testing with reports. Molding capacity runs up to 12-ounce parts on presses up to 150 tons.

Customers span aviation, industrial, consumer, medical, robotics, aerospace, military, sensor, and UAV/UAS sectors. The company works with electronic component distributors such as TTI and Heilind, and with OEMs including LightSpeed Technologies, Forest Dental, Engle Dental Systems, and Warn Industries.

Q&D emphasizes a quality-first culture backed by AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 certification and IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship compliance. Its differentiators include lean manufacturing expertise, quick-turn flexibility, engineering and design-for-manufacturability support, and a supply chain stocked with major connector brands. The rework and fulfillment offering addresses engineering-change orders and non-conforming product already in the supply chain.

Quality Switchgear Inc. is based in Valley View, Texas. The company was founded in 1996 by brothers John and Billy Cope, with Kim Duvall joining as the first employee and office manager. More than two decades later, all three remain with the business, which now employs around 20 people.

The firm operates as a distributor and service provider for electrical switchgear and circuit breaker components. Its inventory spans new, reconditioned, obsolete, and hard-to-find parts from brands such as Eaton, Square D, General Electric, Cutler-Hammer, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Westinghouse, ITE, Merlin Gerin, and Pringle. In addition to supplying bolted-pressure and high-pressure contact switches, motor-control parts, and mounting hardware, Quality Switchgear offers identification, testing, and repair services for circuit breakers, backed by 24/7 phone support.

Customers include industrial factories and plants where switchgear uptime is critical, as well as data-center operators such as Digital Realty. The company’s focus on rapid response—often delivering a replacement breaker within hours—supports facilities that cannot afford extended downtime.

Quality Switchgear traces its origin to the founders’ desire to solve customers’ urgent electrical-parts problems. The original team’s continued involvement and round-the-clock availability are presented as the core reasons clients return.

Qualus was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota. The company operates as a pure-play power infrastructure services firm with additional offices across the United States and Canada, including a headquarters and relay training lab in Lake Mary, Florida.

The firm delivers end-to-end power infrastructure solutions spanning advisory and planning, engineering, program management, energy efficiency, applied solutions, and specialized field services. Qualus supports transmission line and substation design, distribution network resilience, underground distribution, DER/renewables/microgrid integration, mission-critical power, and power generation lifecycle support. The company maintains a multi-state footprint with offices and shops in over 20 locations, plus operations in British Columbia and Ontario.

Qualus serves utilities, generation and energy storage operators, commercial and industrial facilities, data centers, and government agencies. Qualus emphasizes a safety-first culture in which every employee holds stop-work authority, underpinned by human performance principles. Quality assurance and control are executed through independent design reviews, equipment inspections, audits, and a repository of standardized procedures. The firm publishes a sustainability report and positions its purpose-driven capabilities around the energy transition and grid resilience.
